info.adv_downbeats_text: Detects every beat and also the “1” of every bar (downbeat).
info.adv_formats_text: The server reads MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, AAC/M4A and more at full resolution; the original file stays unchanged.
info.adv_meter_text: BeatAnalyzer counts the beats between the downbeats (e.g. 4/4, 3/4); “Smoothing” spaces the bars evenly.
info.adv_robust_text: The transformer listens to the whole excerpt and copes with syncopation, swing and tempo changes (no DBN post-processing).
info.beat_this_text: Developed at Johannes Kepler University Linz (CP JKU) by Francesco Foscarin, Jan Schlüter and Gerhard Widmer (ISMIR 2024). Code and model under the MIT licence – commercial use allowed.
info.md_text: By Francesco Foscarin, Filip Korzeniowski and Richard Vogl (ISMIR 2026). May only be used for non-commercial purposes with attribution (CC BY-NC 4.0). BeatAnalyzer contains neither its code nor its weights; install it by hand into the venv (Linux/macOS: venv/bin/pip; needs PyTorch and ffmpeg):
info.step1_text: The local server reads the file and computes a spectrogram from it.
info.step2_text: beat_this computes for every frame (20 ms) the probability of a beat and of a downbeat.
info.step3_text: The peaks of the curves become beats and downbeats; bars, tempo and time signature follow from them. Without a server the browser makes a rough analysis.
info.title: Models and how it works

metrics.tip_bpm: Beats Per Minute (BPM): Speed of the pulse. Typical ranges: 70–95 BPM (Hip-Hop/ballad), 115–135 BPM (Pop/House/Techno), 160+ BPM (DnB).
metrics.tip_meter: Time signature (e.g. 4/4 = 4 beats per bar, 3/4 = waltz). “% of bars” shows how consistently that bar length holds across the track.
metrics.tip_bars: Number of full bars (each starting on beat “1”) and total detected beats in the song.
metrics.tip_stability: How steady the spacing between beats is: >92% = click-track tight, 80–92% = natural human groove, <80% = tempo drift or uneven tracking.
metrics.tip_ibi: Average gap between consecutive beats in milliseconds (e.g. 500 ms = 120 BPM).
metrics.tip_audio: Total track length and sample rate of the decoded audio (44.1 kHz = CD standard, 48 kHz = video/studio standard).
metrics.jitter_tip: How much the gaps between the beats wobble (standard deviation; missing beats and tempo changes left out). Below about ±10 ms the markers sit frame-exact in a 25/30 fps timeline; more means a live feel – or a grid that is off in places.

tempo.title: Tempo
tempo.help_summary: Shows whether the beat grid runs steady through the whole song. Steady means: the markers stay on the beat even far from the start.
tempo.help_item1: Flat line on the dashed average (Ø): steady tempo (studio, click track) – you can cut by counting bars.
tempo.help_item2: Waves or steps: a live band or a real tempo change. Rose dots = the “1” of each bar; check the markers by ear in these parts.
tempo.help_tip: Tip: a sudden jump to exactly half or double the tempo means the analysis counted wrong there – fix it with Tempo ½× / 2× for that section in “Beat evidence & grid fixes”.
tempo.tip_range: Lowest and highest tempo, and the average (Ø). Only 1–3 BPM apart: the song keeps its tempo – ideal for cutting on the grid.

wave.daf_none: No DAF for this analysis: no continuous downbeat curve.
wave.loupe_only_overview: Magnifier only when at least {sec} s are shown
wave.loupe_paused: Magnifier paused while less than {sec} s are shown – active again when zooming out (click to turn off)

wave.overview_drag: Drag the blue frame to move · click outside to jump
wave.quick_too_short: The track is shorter than {sec} seconds
wave.title: Waveform & beat grid
wave.help_summary: Your main tool for placing cuts: every line is a place where a cut lands on the beat.
wave.help_item1: Rose line with number = the “1” of a bar – the strongest cut point (new scene, hard cut). Cyan lines = beats 2–4, for faster cut rhythms.
wave.help_item2: Dashed amber = the model is unsure here (below 60 %). Check these spots by ear before you cut on them.
wave.help_item3: BAF / DAF at the bottom: how sure the model is of a beat (cyan) or a “1” (rose) at each moment – high peaks are clear hits.
wave.help_tip: Tip: zoom to 5–15 s or use the magnifier. A line should sit on the start of the kick or snare, not after it. If all lines are a little early or late, fix it in “Beat evidence & grid fixes”.
wave.edit_hint: Shift+click: add beat · Alt+click: remove beat

spectrum.live_idle: Press play – the live spectrum moves with the music

evidence.title: Beat Evidence & Grid Fixes
evidence.subtitle: Is the “1” in the right place? Check it and fix it with one click
evidence.verdict_ok: Kick focus on beat {beat} · downbeat phase looks solid
evidence.verdict_shifted_backbeat: Strongest low punch on beat {beat} · backbeat (2 & 4) may be swapped
evidence.verdict_shifted_offbeat: Strongest low punch on off-beat (+0.5) · grid may be shifted by ½ beat
evidence.verdict_flat: Even / subtle kick distribution – verify downbeat by ear
evidence.verdict_insufficient: Too few complete bars to average
evidence.fix_help: Fixes common phase or half-beat grid offsets globally across waveform, metronome, and DaVinci Resolve exports without editing individual beats.
evidence.fix_half_beat_prev_tip: Shifts every beat backward by half a beat (earlier)
evidence.fix_half_beat_next_tip: Shifts every beat forward by half a beat (later)
evidence.fix_tempo_tip: Halves or doubles beat density if the model tracked double- or half-time
evidence.fix_reset_tip: Reset: Restore all bar, grid, and tempo adjustments back to the original analysis in one click
evidence.help_lanes_summary: The part of the song shown in the waveform, split into three bands: shows where the hits are, so you can see whether the lines sit on them.
evidence.help_lanes_1: Spikes = hits: Low (kick, bass), Mid (snare, claps, vocals), High (hi-hats). A cut on a spike feels “on the beat”.
evidence.help_lanes_2: Soft shade behind = sustained sound (bass notes, pads, vocals) – not a cut point.
evidence.help_lanes_tip: Tip: the rose lines should sit on the Low spikes (kick on the “1”). If they sit between the spikes, the grid is shifted.
evidence.help_folded_summary: All bars stacked onto one: shows at a glance whether the “1” is where the kick is – that is, whether your bar markers are right.
evidence.help_folded_1: Rose (Low): kick and bass. In most pop, rock and hip-hop the tallest rose peak is on 1. In house and techno (kick on every beat) it is even – then the folded bar cannot decide, trust your ear.
evidence.help_folded_2: Cyan / indigo: snare and hi-hats – in 4/4 usually on 2 and 4. Amber ticks mark the “and” between the beats.
evidence.help_folded_tip: Tip: tallest rose peak on 2 or 4 → “−1 / +1 beat”; on an amber tick → “−½ / +½ beat”. Or simply take the suggestion on the right.
evidence.help_tempo_summary: How often each tempo occurs: one tall bar means one steady tempo for the whole song.
evidence.help_tempo_1: Cyan: the main tempo. One narrow, tall bar = steady grid, you can trust the markers everywhere.
evidence.help_tempo_2: Rose bar, or bars near the amber lines (½× / 2×): part of the song was counted at half or double speed, or the tempo really changes.
evidence.help_tempo_tip: Tip: find that part in the tempo curve on the left (click to jump there) and fix it there.
evidence.tip_tempo_primary: The most common tempo. Above about 85 %: the grid is steady across the song.
evidence.tip_tempo_bimodal: A second tempo – a real tempo change or a part counted at half or double speed. Look for it in the tempo curve.
evidence.fix_meter_tip: {n} beats per bar: every {n}th beat from the first “1” becomes a “1”
evidence.fix_count_tip: Corrections stay when you move Smoothing; Undo removes the last step, Reset all of them.
evidence.lanes_resize: Drag to change the height (up to 2×); double-click: normal height
evidence.scope_fix_section_tip: Fixes only the beats in the blue frame of the overview – e.g. ½× only where the model counted double.
evidence.scope_fix_need_zoom: Zoom in or move the blue frame first to fix only a section
evidence.suggest_unclear: No clear kick pattern – no suggestion, check by ear
evidence.suggest_tip: BeatAnalyzer tried the combinations of bar start, half beat, beats per bar and tempo on the folded bar. This one puts the kick most clearly on the “1” (and in 4/4 the snare on 2 and 4). Listen before you export – Undo takes it back.

structure.title: Song structure & live
structure.subtitle: Where the song changes – and where you are while listening
structure.help_summary: Loudness per bar over the whole song. Where the sound changes clearly (intro → verse, build-up → drop, chorus → break), BeatAnalyzer marks a section change – always on a “1”, because that is where a cut on the change belongs.
structure.help_1: Green ▲: the song gets louder or fuller (chorus, drop) – a strong place for a hard cut or a new scene.
structure.help_2: Blue ▼: the song gets quieter (break, bridge, outro) – good for calm shots, slow motion or a fade. Violet ◆: the sound changes at about the same loudness.
structure.help_3: Amber line: playhead. Yellow flags: your cue marks.
structure.help_tip: Click the strip or a section button to jump to the “1” there. Section changes go into the DaVinci Resolve export as purple markers. They are a guide from the levels, not a musical analysis – listen before you rely on them.
structure.none: Too few bars for a song structure
structure.chip_tip: {bars} bars – click to jump to the “1”

live.title: Live (while playing)
live.help_summary: Follows the playback: bar counter and the next section – so you can count along while listening and catch cut points without stopping.
live.help_1: Bar counter (can be hidden): the current bar and its beats lit in turn, the “1” in rose; below, the next section and how many bars until it starts.
live.help_2: Spectrum: kick (rose), snare (cyan), hi-hats (indigo); the glow flashes on every beat, stronger on the “1”. If kick and flash do not land together, the grid is off.
live.help_tip: Tip: press M at a cut point while listening – the cue lands on the nearest beat.
live.counter_show_tip: Show the bar counter left of the spectrum
live.counter_hide_tip: Hide the bar counter – the spectrum takes the full width

cue.title: Cue marks
cue.add_tip: Sets a cue on the beat nearest to the playhead (key M; Shift+M: on the nearest “1”)
cue.help_summary: Mark cut points while listening, without stopping: press M where you want a cut. The mark snaps to the nearest beat, so it is on the beat in Resolve too.
cue.help_1: M = nearest beat, Shift+M = nearest “1” (start of the bar).
cue.help_2: Cues appear as yellow flags in the strip and as yellow buttons in the row below, between the sections. They go into the DaVinci Resolve export as yellow markers named “Cue 1”, “Cue 2” … and into the Audacity labels.
cue.help_tip: Tip: rather press a little early than late – the mark snaps to the nearest beat. Click a cue to jump there, × removes it. Cues follow grid fixes.
cue.name: Cue {n}

layout.grip_tip: Drag to move the panel (or arrow keys ↑ ↓ on this grip)
